slides.text: Most new gardeners don't underwater. <hl>They overwater.</hl>

slides.heading: The <hl>Finger Test</hl>
slides.body: Push a finger into the soil up to the second knuckle. Dry down there? Water. Still damp? Wait a day and check again.

slides.heading: Water <hl>Deep</hl>, Not Often
slides.body: A slow, thorough soak every few days grows deeper roots than a quick splash every day. Roots follow the water down.

slides.heading: Aim for the <hl>Soil</hl>
slides.body: Water the base of the plant, not the leaves. Wet leaves in cool weather invite mildew — especially in our foggy Alameda mornings.

slides.heading: Pots Dry <hl>Faster</hl>
items: Check containers more often than beds
Make sure every pot has a drainage hole
A saucer full of water for days = too much

slides.heading: Still Not Sure? <hl>Ask Jason.</hl>
slides.body: Bring your watering questions to our free, in-person class — every two weeks at Makerfarm in Alameda. Leave with a plan for your own space.

caption.instagram:
Most new gardeners don't underwater. They overwater. 💧

A simple rule that helps: push a finger into the soil to the second knuckle. Dry? Water deeply. Damp? Wait. Pots dry out faster than beds, so check those more often.

Got a plant you can't figure out? Bring it to our free, in-person gardening class with Jason — every two weeks at Makerfarm in Alameda. Register at the link in our bio.
